races.name: Westcare Home Care Claiming Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bryson
runners_data.note: Hasn't won in this trip range and drops back slightly in distance here; a true hold-up horse forced wider in the pack due to the crowded rear — amateur jockey Joshua Halford adds to the task, and six wins from similar good-ground profiles in history don't flatter recent form of B6-U26.|

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old on the back end of his career with decent placed form on good ground (0W3P in similar going), but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role that doesn't suit, and the recent P-920P form string is not encouraging at OR 105.|

runners_data.name: Raydamann
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old has winning form on good ground over today's trip and is the lone pace-maker here, giving James Smith (5) complete control of the race on a track that rewards front-runners; the OR 115 mark and recent hurdles win back this up.|

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 17f at OR levels close to today's and has genuine class (1W2P sim-going) — a natural hold-up horse who will be hunting from midfield given the congested rear, but Karl Thornton's runner has the form to get there if the pace is honest.|

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue tie, is trained by Denis Hogan (2/28 in 14 days, showing form), and has a solid OR 120 ceiling; consistent on good ground in flat races but the hurdles form (00/R6-) is patchy and the step up from 12f trips in recent runs to 18f today is notable.|

runners_data.name: Warm In Gorey
runners_data.note: Seven places from 12 sim-going runs tells a story of consistency without winning — a genuine hold-up type bumped into a midfield slot here, wearing a hood; P J Rothwell has two winners in 14 days but Warm In Gorey's top OR finish is 3rd and the 2m2f on sharp Sligo is genuinely within range.|

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Elliott's second string here; at 146lbs and OR 115 with a win on good ground, this seven-year-old travels far enough back to be a potential closer but the F (fell) in recent form and patchy jumping record (P-48F0) raise a safety flag over hurdles.|

runners_data.name: Oh So Charming
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old lightly raced on good ground (14/15 sim-going runs on similar surface) with a win and four places in that band — bumped forward from a natural rear position into a contested midfield slot, and Declan Queally has two winners in 14 days which is a small positive.|

runners_data.name: Slowdownbarney
runners_data.note: The lowest OR in the field at 88 and a form string of 8/080 paints a grim picture; a 5-year-old still learning who has only four sim-going runs and zero wins or places — wears tongue tie and visor, and is mapped well forward of his natural position.|

runners_data.name: Truckers Cruising
runners_data.note: Elliott's third runner and the least fancied with a form string of U6-0P0 and two consecutive blank runs over today's trip on good ground — the 9-day turnaround is notably short and OR 92 is the second lowest in the field; jockey Sam Ewing takes the mount.|

races.paceDynamic: Raydamann is the sole confirmed pace-setter and will lead from the front on what shapes up as a controlled, uncontested gallop around Sligo's sharp 2m2f circuit. With no other confirmed front-runner to challenge him, James Smith can dictate precisely on what fractions he likes, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out or exploit hold-up horses who will struggle to close on good ground at this track. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Rich Belief, Presenting Lad, Warm In Gorey, Oh So Charming, Slowdownbarney and Truckers Cruising are all true hold-up horses compressed into midfield slots, meaning few if any will get a clean draw of the race from where they want to be. Howdoyalikeherhome and God Of Thunder represent the genuine hold-up presences further back, though the former's jumping has been inconsistent. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit handy just off Raydamann and travel with him into the straight, rather than deep closers who will need a proper end-to-end gallop that never materialises.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Raydamann Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Raydamann is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control the tempo at his own pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Raydamann sets a measured gallop that ensures the race is truly run to his strengths, turning for home with a decisive advantage over those coming from off the pace on good ground where closing is hard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit The Front
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling prominently or in midfield makes a bold move from the home bend and overhauling the leader before the last.
scenarios.body: Rich Belief or God Of Thunder — both with some form on good — get into a rhythm closer to the pace than their natural style and arrive with a challenge that Raydamann cannot repel on the short Sligo straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Unravels Raydamann
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely honest enough that Raydamann weakens in the home straight and a hold-up type picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Howdoyalikeherhome or Warm In Gorey — both proven over similar distances on good ground — could stay on late if Raydamann has over-committed, though this requires a tempo that looks unlikely given the lack of pace pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution chaos means several horses race awkwardly wide or prominently, fragmenting the pace and creating a falsely run race that a late swoop resolves.
scenarios.body: With six hold-up types forced to race against their nature, a genuine late-running chance for Bryson or Oh So Charming could emerge if the race descends into a messy scramble, though style-fit concerns and the track's short home straight make this genuinely unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Raydamann's jumping efficiency will be critical — if James Smith (5) meets any hurdle wrong early and loses momentum, the race shape that his front-running role creates collapses entirely and several compressed midfield horses rush into a tactical vacuum.

Rich Belief has legitimate good-ground form at this level (1W2P) and is racing out of his natural hold-up role — if he gets a clean jumping round and travels prominently rather than deep, he carries a genuine each-way threat that the raw style mapping undersells.

Howdoyalikeherhome's jumping record (fall in recent form) is a live safety concern at the hurdles — Josh Williamson (5) is a conditional jockey on a horse that has shown tendency to blunder, and at Sligo's tight circuit that could affect several runners bunched closely.

God Of Thunder's stepping up sharply in trip from recent 12f handicaps to 2m2f today — Denis Hogan's runner has never demonstrated staying ability at this distance on the hurdles course and that unproven stamina profile should temper any price shortening.|

Six confirmed hold-up types redistributed into midfield create meaningful traffic risk between the first and second hurdle as the field fans — horses drawn wide or slow into the first hurdle could interfere, and Slowdownbarney (visor, 5yo, lowest OR) is most likely to be the source of early crowding.|

races.name: Martin Reilly Hyundai Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: An Lachin Beag
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 223 days off for Nigel Slevin, with a win on Good ground and a third at Goodwood on similar footing last time; the long absence is the main query but the style and going conditions suit perfectly.

runners_data.name: Circus Hill
runners_data.note: Consistent form horse with five consecutive placings on Good ground for Mark McNiff, though its natural hold-up style means it will be racing in a more forward position than ideal in this crowded field — Phillip Enright will need to produce it from a compromised spot.

runners_data.name: Glendaars Crystal
runners_data.note: Tagged as a finisher who fades late, which is a concerning double negative — a hold-up horse with a fade flag is squeezed into midfield here and has posted three unplaced efforts on Good ground with no wins or places to date.

runners_data.name: I Dont Really Care
runners_data.note: 229 days off the track is a significant absence, and this horse's natural rearward style will be further cramped by the crowded hold-up section; the fade flag compounds the concern in what is already a structurally awkward scenario for closers.

runners_data.name: Idaho Expresso
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with headgear, but the fade flag and two unplaced runs on Good ground over 20f suggest the step back to 2m2f at Sligo might suit marginally; the risk is a duel with Speisialta draining it before the finish.

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with an entirely flat-track Flat background — all five previous runs came on Standard or similar AW/Flat surfaces at short distances; hurdles over 2m2f on turf looks a significant ask on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Saoirses Choice
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a fourth on Soft and ninth on Good, naturally pushed into midfield here; Alix Balfe (7lb claim) is an angle for connections, and the form at 16f on Good is at least competitive for this grade.

runners_data.name: Sea Feliz
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained and Danny Mullins in the saddle gives this debutante strong connective tissue, but a single run showing tenth over 20f on Good is the only evidence and the fade flag gives pause; the yard's strike rate (17/62 in 14 days) is the headline angle.

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: Front-runner with headgear returning just 14 days after its last run, which is a positive freshness angle for Anthony Black's yard; four-figure form includes a fourth on Soft and a Refused — the key is whether it can sustain the lead against Idaho Expresso without blowing up.

runners_data.name: Kilgharrahs Love
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with flat-track form on Soft and Standard surfaces, naturally a hold-up type displaced into midfield by the sheer volume of closers in this field; the going and distance are both unexplored territory at this level.

runners_data.name: Maroel
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — no form string, no last-run date, debut runner for Maike Magnussen with Conor Clarke (7lb claim) up; style classified as unknown and going experience absent, making this a pure wildcard in an otherwise form-readable race.

runners_data.name: Moonwing
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with a single run showing eleventh on Good over 17f, naturally a hold-up type with the fade flag attached; Paul Gilligan's yard running at 1/14 in the last fortnight provides a minor stable angle but the form evidence is thin.

runners_data.name: My Elusive Mate
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's entry has the most significant trainer backing in the race (1/44 in 14 days) and races prominently — seventh and fifth on Good at 16f for Sam Ewing suggests it handles the going and can travel close enough to the pace to be involved late.

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta and Idaho Expresso are the two confirmed front-runners and will dispute the lead from the outset over Sligo's tight 2m2f trip on Good ground, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a solo dawdle. With both horses carrying headgear and both having form that suggests they fade in the finish (Idaho Expresso specifically tagged), the question is whether they burn each other out or one settles into a rhythm and dictates. An Lachin Beag and My Elusive Mate are the natural prominent horses capable of tracking the pace and pouncing if the leaders tie each other up, and this contested-pace shape is most likely to suit a prominent racer who can sit just off the heat and produce a clean finish. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Kilgharrahs Love, Circus Hill, I Dont Really Care, and Glendaars Crystal are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield slots they won't naturally occupy — meaning the backfield will be crowded and a late swooping finish is structurally harder to deliver. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel within striking range of a contested pace are most favoured, with true hold-up horses facing a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta and Idaho Expresso press each other through the early and middle stages, draining each other's reserves before the home turn.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners empty each other out racing into the final bend, leaving a prominent stalker with a clear, uncontested run to the line on the Good ground. An Lachin Beag and My Elusive Mate are ideally positioned to capitalise, travelling just behind the battle and striking on the descent.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Idaho Expresso or Speisialta gains a clear lead early and the other is taken back or drops away, allowing a solo gallop at a sustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: One pacemaker controls on the front end without serious pressure, setting a rhythm that suits their profile and potentially giving them enough in reserve to hold on at a small track like Sligo with its tight bends. Idaho Expresso has the headgear angle but the fade flag tempers expectations; Speisialta is the more likely candidate to settle and hold.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly searching and the front-runners burn out enough to allow a strong-finishing hold-up type to close late despite the crowded midfield.
scenarios.body: Circus Hill has the most credible form in this race — five runs showing consistent placing on Good ground — and if it can navigate from its remapped midfield position to find a run, it becomes the most dangerous closer. Glendaars Crystal and I Dont Really Care face the same structural challenge given the crowded hold-up section, making this a lower-probability outcome despite the form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Lottery, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace causes bunching and interference, opening the race up for a lightly raced or unexposed type to emerge from a clean passage.
scenarios.body: Maroel is completely unknown on debut and Sea Feliz has Mullins' backing on a single run, and either could outclass this modest field if the pace scenario creates chaos in the pack. Moonwing and Kilgharrahs Love are both lightly exposed and could benefit from a muddling race at a small venue.

watchPoints.text: Speisialta and Idaho Expresso — watch whether one immediately dominates the other off the break or whether they run head-to-head, as a genuine duel will be the key pace-shape trigger for the whole race.

Circus Hill — Phillip Enright will need to find daylight from a position further forward than natural; watch for the horse being checked or trapped on the final bend where Sligo's tight circuit creates bottlenecks.

My Elusive Mate — Elliott's runner is the prominent type best placed to exploit a contested pace, but watch whether Sam Ewing can secure a clean position in the early stages before the pace battle unfolds ahead.

Sea Feliz — Danny Mullins on a Mullins-trained debutante always attracts significant market support at Irish tracks; watch the market move pre-race as a proxy for how seriously the stable views its chance on debut.
Maroel — no form or style data available; watch the paddock and opening moves in the early stages to gauge whether this is a serious contender or a track-learning exercise for the yard.

races.name: Kilcawley Construction Rated Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old arrives on a two-from-two winning run over course-and-distance on good ground, Josh Williamson claiming 5lb, and his prominent style positions him perfectly to track Crystabel and strike at the business end.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue rides a horse whose best form has come on good ground over similar trips; he's a genuine prominent racer who will look to sit close to Crystabel's heels and his recent win over 18f good makes him a credible late challenger from this position.

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: John Nallen's six-year-old has solid placed form over this trip and going, carrying headgear; although shown at the rear of the pace map, he is actually a natural prominent type who is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal given the competition for that position ahead of him, which tempers his prospects.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins partners the lone confirmed front-runner, whose C&D win last time out and consistent placed form over this exact course and going make her the controlling influence; uncontested lead on good turf at Sligo is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: Recent form has been modest (8-9740) and his going record at Sligo on good ground is poor (13/13 runs rated); though a natural prominent type, he is mapped to midfield due to congestion ahead of him, and his current form trajectory gives little confidence he can overcome that positional disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Crystabel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, in a five-runner field at Sligo, will dictate comfortably from the front under Danny Mullins without any rival likely to apply genuine early pressure. Manoir De Mirande and Luker's Tipple are both genuine prominent types who will track Crystabel at close range, creating a steady, controlled tempo rather than a gruelling pace battle. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Firebrand and Hillhead Runner are true prominent horses who are likely to find themselves racing a touch further back than ideal, with Manoir De Mirande and Luker's Tipple better placed to enforce their preferred position behind Crystabel. The race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently and travel into the contest, with Crystabel best positioned to control the race and prominent trackers best placed to pounce — true hold-up horses or those pushed out of position are at a clear tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crystabel Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Crystabel dictates an uncontested lead and the field settles into a steady rhythm, allowing her to dominate from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Crystabel sets a sustainable gallop on good ground that suits her, with the prominent pair Manoir De Mirande and Luker's Tipple tracking but never threatening to get past until too late. Her recent win over C&D and strong course-going record make her the default beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Crystabel is reeled in from the second-last hurdle by a better-credentialled prominent racer moving smoothly into contention.
scenarios.body: Manoir De Mirande or Luker's Tipple travel strongly in Crystabel's slipstream and have enough quality to pick her off approaching the final flight on good ground that suits both. Manoir De Mirande's recent course-and-distance form and Elliott yard angle make him the principal threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is faster than expected and Crystabel and the prominent brigade tie each other up, leaving the field vulnerable to a late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Firebrand or Hillhead Runner, both of whom are natural prominent types pushed back on the pace map, producing a genuine late challenge from off the pace — a role that is not natural to either. The discounted style-fit for both runners makes this shape unlikely to materialise in a meaningful way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves too hot for Crystabel and a fresher rival runs her down close home.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop over 2m2f on good ground tests Crystabel's stamina reserves and a prominent tracker, most likely Luker's Tipple, proves the stronger stayer in the closing stages. This shape requires genuine pace pressure which the small field is unlikely to generate, making it a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Crystabel (Danny Mullins) jumps cleanly from the front — if she flukes every hurdle and opens a clear margin by halfway, the field may simply lack the firepower to reel her in before the last.

Manoir De Mirande's position just off Crystabel's quarters is the key tactical battle to monitor — if he travels into contention travelling strongly at the third-last, Elliott's horse becomes the main danger to the leader.

Firebrand and Hillhead Runner are both natural prominent types who may push forward early against expectation, creating unexpected pressure on Crystabel if jockeys try to reclaim their preferred position — watch the first two flights for signs of a pace flare.

Luker's Tipple's rider Keith Donoghue is worth monitoring for how aggressively he positions early — Cromwell's runners often travel prominently and Donoghue may attempt to sit directly on Crystabel's tail rather than give ground to Manoir De Mirande.

With only five runners on good ground at Sligo, the pace is unlikely to be truly strong — races of this profile tend to finish in a rush from the second-last, favouring horses who have settled into a comfortable rhythm rather than those who have fought for position early.

races.name: SIS Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Go To Town
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with good recent form on Good ground (8/9 similar-going), handles this trip well, and Daniel King is a competent pilot; lacks a win from 9 similar-going runs but consistently places, making this a solid each-way profile.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 years with solid prominent-racing profile and six places from 15 Good-ground starts; Sam Ewing takes over for Fitzgerald's yard, which has had no runners in the last 14 days — form at 2m2f Good looks fine but the age may tell in a big competitive field.

runners_data.name: Justicialism
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose recent form shows a string of seconds and thirds — Mr O McGill (5lb claim) adds appeal, and the 15-day turnaround on Good ground suits; has placed in five of nine similar-going runs and could be the most reliable each-way candidate from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Holds-up and finishes into places; tongue-strap fitted, handled Good ground well (9/10 similar-going), but has not won from 10 attempts and the amateur rider (7lb claim) at OR 93 faces a stiff task in a 19-runner field — three places from 10 Good runs suggests honest rather than brilliant.

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good ground last time, making a prominent move from 2m2f in today's conditions very attractive; Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim is a genuine asset and the OR 91 looks fair for a horse whose most recent form shows a win and two places on similar ground.

runners_data.name: Il Pirata
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old prominent racer running for Mrs Lorna Fowler with Mr M J Love (7lb claim); limited Good-ground sample of four runs with zero wins or places, and the 'B' in the form string suggests a jumping mishap — hard to fancy with any confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago (quick turnaround flagged), showed three wins from 15 Good-ground starts, and Ciaran Murphy's yard has a runner in the last 14 days; the 2m2f trip is not his shortest but he handled 2m2f well last time — the fast return may be a fitness play or a concern.

runners_data.name: Mon Sheriffe
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type fitted with a hood; P-U-P recent form is sketchy but P J Rothwell's yard has had two winners in the last 14 days, suggesting yard is in form; only 13 days since last run and limited Good-going sample make him speculative despite the stable angle.

runners_data.name: Moulane West
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old hold-up type fitted with tongue-strap and blinkers; 58 days off the track is a meaningful absence, and while he won once from 15 Good-ground runs his recent finishing positions (9,10,15) suggest he is past his best — the gear change adds mild interest but not enough to overcome the layoff.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won at 2m2f on Good ground and has four places from 15 similar-going starts; Jack Gilligan (5lb claim) for Paul John Gilligan's yard which had a winner in the past 14 days — the hold-up style suits the likely scenario where midfield closers get a clear run late.

runners_data.name: Copper Rocker
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish, which is a significant negative flag at this trip; Danny Mullins is a top-class jockey and may manage the horse's limitations, but OR 89 with zero wins or places from six Good-ground runs and a finishing fade tendency makes this one to oppose rather than support.

runners_data.name: Boltlander
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map due to the volume of rearward types; STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers confidence and recent form (P,0,P,0,P) is uninspiring — Sean Flanagan is capable but the 62-day absence and poor recent record make it hard to construct a winning case even in the most favourable scenario.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare repositioned to midfield on the map given the crowded rear; fades in the finish and recent form shows a 6 as the best recent return — STYLE_FIT 0.93 flags she may race closer than ideal, and Darragh O'Keeffe's class aboard cannot fully compensate for the combination of style displacement and weak recent form.

runners_data.name: Nothing Da Now
runners_data.note: 206 days off the track is the most significant flag here — this hold-up type has been running mainly on Heavy ground and the switch to Good (only 2/6 similar-going) is an additional question mark; naturally at the rear but mapped to midfield, STYLE_FIT 0.90, and the long absence makes this one to leave alone.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Won at OR 78 on Good ground 14 days ago and has a blinkers flag suggesting headgear dependency; Conor Clarke (7lb claim) for Denis Gerard Hogan who has had two winners recently — the form shows a 1 and 8 as latest results, so the previous win was genuine, but this hold-up type displaced to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.92) will need everything to go right in a 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Glenriver
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fitted with a tongue-strap, showing PPP0 in recent starts — finishing positions are consistently poor and the 23-day return does not mask a damning recent record; Shane Crawley's yard had a runner recently but the pattern of form makes this horse one of the race's weakest propositions.

runners_data.name: Stormy Jenn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type running in a hood (hg:p) with a form string including a fall and a P; 23 days between runs and mainly Good-ground experience (12/15) but no wins and only one place — positioned to midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.91) and age combined with poor recent form makes this hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Ripsnorter
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, carrying top weight of 168lbs at OR 99, with a Sligo advantage of being able to control tempo entirely unchallenged — won on Good ground earlier in career and the 16-day turnaround looks fine; the key risk is whether OR 99 top weight tells late against fresher rivals.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type in a hood, displaced to midfield on the map (STYLE_FIT 0.92); Paul W Flynn's yard had a winner in the last 14 days and the 14-day return is acceptable, but only 3/5 similar-going runs and a form string featuring a 17th and 10th suggest she is struggling at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Ripsnorter is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and, with no genuine rival looking to pressurise from the outset, should be able to control tempo from the front at a sustainable, measured gallop on Good ground at Sligo. The prominent runners — Go To Town, General Clermont, Andyourbirdcansing, Steps In The Sand, and Il Pirata — will slot in behind and create a compact, tightly-bunched group through the early stages, meaning the race is unlikely to truly collapse into a crawl even if Ripsnorter dictates. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically sit at the rear in a 19-runner race; Boltlander, Frontier Rose, Nothing Da Now, Backinabit, and others have been redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice several will find themselves racing further forward than their natural style demands. A controlled, single-pace lead with a prominent wall tracking close behind heavily favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than those relying on a late flourish that may never materialise against a measured tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ripsnorter Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter sets a measured, uncontested lead and the prominent trackers pick him off turning for home.
scenarios.body: Ripsnorter dictates a fair but not brutal gallop, and the horses sitting just off the pace — Go To Town, Andyourbirdcansing, Steps In The Sand — are ideally positioned to challenge from the second-last hurdle without needing a gear change they cannot find.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ripsnorter Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady and no prominent rival has the stamina to reel him in over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: Ripsnorter, already on a good day over this 2m2f trip on Good going, is never headed and simply keeps tabs on his rivals' challenges, having conserved energy through his uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the back straight to string the field out and allow a midfield horse to close powerfully into a clear run.
scenarios.body: Justicialism and Georginas Jet, both consistent placers on Good ground, have the profile to stay on strongly when others tire from racing more prominently than intended; the 19-runner field creates enough traffic for a well-angled late move.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Hold-Up Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely prominent-natured horse like Boltlander or Frontier Rose, forced forward by the large field, happens to settle into a better rhythm than their recent form suggests and stays on.
scenarios.body: These horses are racing out of their natural role and their STYLE_FIT discounts temper confidence, but in a large-field handicap the chaos of 19 runners occasionally allows a displaced type to find a line and sustain late effort better than expected.

watchPoints.text: Ripsnorter (sole front-runner) could easily steal this from the front if the prominent trackers — particularly Go To Town and Andyourbirdcansing — fail to close the gap quickly enough from the second-last flight.

Steps In The Sand ran only six days ago — watch for any signs of fatigue in the back straight, as a quick turnaround in a 19-runner field over 2m2f on Good ground could compromise his stamina at the crucial point.

The 19-runner field creates significant traffic risk at the first few hurdles and in the back straight; hold-up types like Justicialism and Georginas Jet need a clean passage — any interference early could ruin their race before it begins.

Nothing Da Now returns after 206 days off the track and has barely raced on Good ground — monitor in the market; if backed despite the absence and going concern, it would represent a strong stable confidence signal worth noting.

Boltlander and Frontier Rose are both flagged as fading types racing out of their natural role; if either drifts back to the very rear from the off rather than tracking midfield as mapped, that is a visual sign the pace scenario is becoming more extreme at the front than the map currently suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Ivana D'alco (Mullins/Hayes) is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously contest that position, will dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits her over this 2m5f trip on Good ground at Sligo. The prominent types — Cut The Rope and Minella Moon Shine — will likely settle just behind her, creating a small, organised lead group rather than a contested pace duel. With a single pace-setter controlling proceedings, the gallop is expected to be measured and sustainable, which compresses the race into a stamina-and-jump contest in the final stages rather than one decided by early positioning. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace and quicken from a prominent position off a steady gallop, rather than true hold-up types who need a genuine end-to-end test to close ground. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the pace map can place at the rear — Turlough Abu is a true hold-up type shuffled into midfield on the map, and Mr Caulfield and Tommy Go Maith are also rearward-inclined — meaning Ivana D'alco and the prominent pair are most likely to actually secure the positions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ivana D'alco controls and wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ivana D'alco leads uncontested, dictates a fair gallop, and her rivals lack the class or late kick to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Hayes settles her cleanly in front, jumps are tidy, and the measured pace suits a horse who can get the trip without being pressured; Mullins' 17/62 T14 strike rate underlines the yard's operational intent.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair overhaul leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ivana D'alco's jumping is untidy or she fades from the second-last, allowing a settled prominent horse to sprint past.
scenarios.body: Cut The Rope (OR 112, Good-going form) or Minella Moon Shine (2nd in similar class on Good) track the pace throughout and find more in the straight on this flat Sligo finish; both have the profile to travel economically and strike late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield closer delivers late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and a progressive hold-up type picks off the tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Fox Walk (unknown style, lightly raced but OR 120, Darragh O'Keeffe booked) or Fuusland (Elliott, recent run 23 days ago) emerge from midfield as the race quickens from the third-last; both are unexposed enough to improve significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True hold-up horse pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the backmarkers — including the redistributed Turlough Abu — get a genuine test that brings them into the race.
scenarios.body: This shape relies on horses racing out of role and is the least likely outcome; Turlough Abu's consistent finishing position (7th-9th in most starts) and fade-in-finish tag make a winning run from truly off the pace improbable.

watchPoints.text: Ivana D'alco's jumping — Hayes will want her fluent throughout; a mistake at any of the final three flights could hand the race to the prominent pair behind.|

Minella Moon Shine's rapid turnaround (ran 2 days ago) is highly unusual and worth flagging — watch market moves for clues as to whether this was a deliberate targeting of today's race or an error in the data.|

Fox Walk is completely unknown stylistically and with a 90-day break; if she settles prominently under O'Keeffe she could easily outrun her odds, making her a danger to the favourite that is hard to price.|

San Patricio has no going history, no form string, and a 3lb claimer — treat any drifting or significant market move with this runner as meaningful information given the near-total absence of public form.|

The cluster of fade-in-finish hold-up horses (Tommy Go Maith, Mr Caulfield, Turlough Abu) is unlikely to be flattered by this pace shape — watch for any of them pulling or jumping sluggishly early, which would confirm the race is playing out as expected.|

races.paceDynamic: Jupiter Du Gite is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 2m5f handicap hurdle and is likely to dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Sligo. Behind him, Littlebiggie, Cornmarket, and Lilac Lady will push for prominent positions, creating a genuine contest for the early berths and ensuring the pace is at least honest if not pressured. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place cleanly at the rear — Run For The Border and Whiskey Serenade are genuine closers by nature but are redistributed to midfield positions because the back of the field is congested with similar profiles, meaning they may not find the clean passage their style demands. With a single unchallenged front-runner setting a controlled tempo over 2m5f on Good turf, this race shape strongly favours prominent horses who can settle just off the pace and pick up momentum from two out — patient hold-up horses will need a genuine injection of pace that may never arrive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite leads unchallenged at a fair pace and one of the prominent trackers produces a clean two-out move.
scenarios.body: Jupiter Du Gite sets a steady fractions across Sligo's undulations, with Littlebiggie, Cornmarket, and Lilac Lady travelling in his slipstream before the race unfolds from the third-last; the prominent runner with the best finishing resources graduates to the front and stays on dourly on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite bowls along at a true gallop and simply outstays his rivals over this demanding 2m5f trip.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to seriously challenge for the lead, Jupiter Du Gite controls every yard and draws on his stamina reserves from the home turn; the absence of any real rival for the front means he conserves enough energy to repel prominent chasers late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace develops into a genuine end-to-end gallop that strings out the field and creates space for a late run.
scenarios.body: You Make Me Smile or In The Minus, settled further back, need a stronger pace than Jupiter Du Gite typically generates to make late ground; this scenario is tempered by the fact that Run For The Border and Whiskey Serenade, the most natural closers, are not guaranteed to find their true rear position and may be caught in traffic mid-pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race turns into a sprint from the final hurdle with minimal early gallop.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race at Sligo over this trip typically produces a bunched, chaotic finish where stamina is neutralised and tactical speed becomes decisive; this benefits nimbler types but is the least likely shape given Jupiter Du Gite's front-running habits and the course's testing nature.

watchPoints.text: Jupiter Du Gite sets the entire pace structure — if he is pressed early by Littlebiggie or Cornmarket for the lead, the tempo increases dramatically and the race shape shifts away from Scenario A toward a more open finish.

Lilac Lady's 15/15 sim-going record on Good turf is the standout statistic in the field — watch for Alan King (7lb) to position her just off Jupiter Du Gite and deliver her run from the third-last hurdle.

Run For The Border and Whiskey Serenade are genuine hold-up horses who may find mid-pack positions congested; if either is blocked turning for home rather than producing their run from the back, their chance evaporates regardless of form.

Bruant has a fade-in-finish flag and is trained by AJ Martin who has had 2 winners from 10 in the last 14 days — watch whether the yard's current form outweighs the runner's own tendency to empty late over this demanding 2m5f on Good ground.

Cornmarket has had only 8 days between runs and a wide form range including a fall and a last-place finish — watch in the market for any drift that signals the yard is managing fitness rather than targeting this race seriously.
